rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: In emergency settings, most people experience psychological distress (e.g. sadness, fear, anger).
rows.ne: आपत्कालीन परिस्थितिमा अधिकांश मानिसहरूले मानसिक व्यथा अनुभव गर्छन् (जस्तै, दुःख, डर, रिस)।
rows.bt: In emergency situations, most people experience mental distress (for example, sadness, fear, anger).
rows.note: Uses the supplied unvalidated candidates for emergency settings and psychological distress, retaining sadness, fear and anger as examples.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: Most affected individuals will gradually start to feel better, especially if they use helpful ways of coping with stress and receive support from their families and communities.
rows.ne: असर परेका अधिकांश व्यक्तिहरूलाई बिस्तारै राम्रो महसुस हुन थाल्नेछ, विशेष गरी उनीहरूले तनावको सामना गर्ने सहयोगी तरिकाहरू अपनाएमा र आफ्ना परिवार तथा समुदायबाट सहयोग पाएमा।
rows.bt: Most affected individuals will gradually begin to feel better, especially if they adopt helpful ways of coping with stress and receive support from their families and communities.
rows.note: The coping wording is an unvalidated draft without a supplied frozen equivalent; the majority, gradual improvement and especially-if condition are retained.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: Disseminating key messages can encourage positive coping, help-seeking and support for people experiencing distress.
rows.ne: मुख्य सन्देशहरू प्रसार गर्नाले सकारात्मक ढङ्गले सामना गर्ने तरिका अपनाउन, सहयोग खोज्न र व्यथा अनुभव गरिरहेका मानिसहरूलाई सहयोग गर्न प्रोत्साहन मिल्न सक्छ।
rows.bt: Disseminating key messages can encourage adopting positive ways of coping, seeking support and supporting people who are experiencing distress.
rows.note: Positive coping and help-seeking are drafted without supplied frozen equivalents; the source expresses a possibility, not a guaranteed effect.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: Key messages may be newly developed for the specific emergency and context or may be adapted from a pool of existing key messages.
rows.ne: मुख्य सन्देशहरू कुनै विशेष आपत्कालीन अवस्था र सन्दर्भका लागि नयाँ रूपमा विकास गर्न सकिन्छ वा विद्यमान मुख्य सन्देशहरूको सङ्ग्रहबाट अनुकूलन गर्न सकिन्छ।
rows.bt: Key messages can be developed anew for a particular emergency situation and context or adapted from an existing collection of key messages.
rows.note: The recurring standalone term key messages is absent from the glossary; proposed form: [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence], consistent with the supplied activity label.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: Key messaging should be simple, focused and concrete and should help people to understand normal and common stress reactions, communicate an expectancy of resilience, emphasize culturally and age-appropriate coping mechanisms, discourage harmful ways of coping (e.g. heavy alcohol use) and include information on how and where to access MHPSS services and support.
rows.ne: मुख्य सन्देशहरू सरल, केन्द्रित र ठोस हुनुपर्छ र तिनले मानिसहरूलाई तनावप्रति देखिने सामान्य प्रतिक्रियाहरू तथा तनावप्रति प्रायः देखिने प्रतिक्रियाहरू बुझ्न सघाउनुपर्छ, उत्थानशीलताको अपेक्षा व्यक्त गर्नुपर्छ, संस्कृति र उमेरअनुकूल सामना गर्ने उपायहरूमा जोड दिनुपर्छ, सामना गर्ने हानिकारक तरिकाहरूलाई निरुत्साहित गर्नुपर्छ (जस्तै, अत्यधिक मदिरा सेवन) र MHPSS सेवा तथा सहयोग कसरी र कहाँ प्राप्त गर्ने भन्ने जानकारी समावेश गर्नुपर्छ।
rows.bt: Key messages should be simple, focused and concrete, and they should help people understand normal reactions seen in response to stress and reactions frequently seen in response to stress, express an expectation of resilience, emphasize coping measures suited to culture and age, discourage harmful ways of coping (for example, excessive alcohol consumption) and include information on how and where to obtain MHPSS services and support.
rows.note: The frozen candidates for common stress reactions and resilience are retained; coping terminology remains an unvalidated draft without a supplied frozen equivalent.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: Review relevant information (e.g. existing key messages for specific groups on relevant topics) and messaging efforts already in place (e.g. by other humanitarian actors) to aid planning and coordination (e.g. through MHPSS TWGs).43
rows.ne: योजना र समन्वयमा सहयोग पुर्‍याउन (जस्तै, MHPSS TWGs मार्फत) सान्दर्भिक जानकारी (जस्तै, सम्बन्धित विषयमा विशेष समूहहरूका लागि तयार गरिएका विद्यमान मुख्य सन्देशहरू) र पहिलेदेखि भइरहेका सन्देश प्रसारका प्रयासहरू (जस्तै, अन्य मानवीय कार्यमा संलग्न पक्षहरूबाट भइरहेका प्रयासहरू) को समीक्षा गर्नुहोस्।43
rows.bt: Review relevant information (e.g., existing key messages prepared for specific groups on related topics) and ongoing message dissemination efforts (e.g., efforts by other actors involved in humanitarian work) to help with planning and coordination (e.g., through MHPSS TWGs).43
rows.note: Key messages uses the proposed standalone form [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]. MHPSS TWGs and footnote marker 43 are retained without expansion.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: Collaboratively develop/identify, adapt and translate culturally relevant key messages with targeted groups (e.g. through participatory discussions with community members of different ages and genders, people with disabilities and other diverse characteristics, and other relevant stakeholders such as persons working in health, protection or education settings, government actors, faith-based actors, and persons with lived experience of mental health conditions; see also actions on community engagement in MSP activity 2.1).44
rows.ne: लक्षित समूहहरूसँग सहकार्य गर्दै सांस्कृतिक रूपमा सान्दर्भिक मुख्य सन्देशहरू तयार गर्नुहोस्/पहिचान गर्नुहोस्, अनुकूलन गर्नुहोस् र अनुवाद गर्नुहोस् (उदाहरणका लागि, विभिन्न उमेर र लैङ्गिक समूहका समुदायका सदस्यहरू, अपाङ्गता भएका व्यक्तिहरू तथा अन्य विविध विशेषताहरू भएका व्यक्तिहरू र स्वास्थ्य, संरक्षण वा शिक्षाका क्षेत्रमा काम गर्ने व्यक्तिहरू, सरकारका सम्बद्ध पक्षहरू, आस्थामा आधारित सम्बद्ध पक्षहरू तथा आफैँले मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी अवस्थाहरू अनुभव गरेका व्यक्तिहरू जस्ता अन्य सान्दर्भिक सरोकारवालाहरूसँग सहभागीमूलक छलफलमार्फत; MSP गतिविधि 2.1 मा सामुदायिक सहभागितासम्बन्धी कार्यहरू पनि हेर्नुहोस्)44।
rows.bt: Working together with target groups, prepare/identify, adapt and translate culturally relevant key messages (for example, through participatory discussions with community members of different age and gender groups, persons with disabilities and persons with other diverse characteristics, and other relevant stakeholders such as people working in health, protection or education, relevant government parties, faith-based parties and people who have themselves experienced mental health conditions; also see the tasks related to community participation in MSP activity 2.1)44.
rows.note: The lived-experience wording refers to people who have themselves experienced mental health conditions; activity reference 2.1 and footnote marker 44 are retained.

rows.en: Get community feedback on communication materials and messages before and after dissemination, and check accuracy and appropriateness of translations.

rows.bt: Obtain feedback from the community on communication materials and messages before and after dissemination, and check the accuracy and appropriateness of translations.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: Disseminate key messages together with community members and other humanitarian actors using media appropriate to the context, considering culture, literacy, accessibility and access to technology (e.g. discussion sessions, posters, information leaflets, radio messaging, social media campaigns, videos, community theatre, comic strips, digital tools such as chatbots).45
rows.ne: संस्कृति, साक्षरता, पहुँचयोग्यता र प्रविधिमा पहुँचलाई ध्यानमा राखी, सन्दर्भअनुकूल माध्यमहरू प्रयोग गरेर समुदायका सदस्यहरू र अन्य मानवीय कार्यमा संलग्न पक्षहरूसँग मिलेर मुख्य सन्देशहरू प्रसार गर्नुहोस् (जस्तै, छलफल सत्र, पोस्टर, जानकारीमूलक पर्चा, रेडियोमार्फत सन्देश प्रसार, सामाजिक सञ्जाल अभियान, भिडियो, सामुदायिक नाटक, चित्रकथाका शृङ्खला र च्याटबटजस्ता डिजिटल उपकरण)।45
rows.bt: Taking culture, literacy, accessibility and access to technology into account, disseminate key messages together with community members and other actors involved in humanitarian work, using context-appropriate means (e.g., discussion sessions, posters, informational leaflets, message dissemination through radio, social media campaigns, videos, community drama, series of picture stories and digital tools such as chatbots).45
rows.note: Key messages uses the proposed standalone form [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]. Accessibility is expressed as a noun; T078 is not listed because its exact supplied form is not used. Footnote marker 45 is retained.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: Develop larger participatory campaigns in multiple accessible formats to promote the mental health and psychosocial well-being of persons with mental health conditions, to promote and protect their rights (e.g. inclusion and access to services and opportunities) and to highlight their capacities.
rows.ne: मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी अवस्थाहरू भएका व्यक्तिहरूको मानसिक स्वास्थ्य र मनोसामाजिक कल्याण प्रवर्द्धन गर्न, उनीहरूका अधिकारहरू (जस्तै, समावेशिता तथा सेवा र अवसरहरूमा पहुँच) प्रवर्द्धन र संरक्षण गर्न तथा उनीहरूका क्षमताहरू उजागर गर्न विभिन्न पहुँचयोग्य ढाँचाहरूमा अझ ठूला सहभागीमूलक अभियानहरू तयार गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Prepare larger participatory campaigns in various accessible formats to promote the mental health and psychosocial well-being of persons with mental health conditions, to promote and protect their rights (for example, inclusion and access to services and opportunities) and to bring their abilities to light.
rows.note: The instruction retains all three purposes: promoting mental health and psychosocial well-being, promoting and protecting rights, and highlighting capacities.

rows.section: Section 3 > 3.3 Disseminate key messages to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being
rows.en: 43 Collaboration with social and behavioural change (SBC) specialists can improve the effectiveness of messaging campaigns and other MHPSS activities. SBC involves using social science and evidence to understand and address the cognitive, social and structural factors that shape behaviour and social norms. Using different approaches, such as communication, social mobilization and community engagement, SBC teams collaborate with community members to understand attitudes, beliefs and behaviours and to promote positive change, collect feedback, address rumours, and co-design solutions, while reinforcing communities’ empowerment and ownership. For example, online and offline ‘social listening’/feedback exercises are conducted to identify concerns, information gaps, existing sources of support, and coping mechanisms. SBCC is sometimes known as Communication for Development (C4D), Communicating With Communities (CWC), and Community Engagement & Accountability.
rows.ne: 43 सामाजिक तथा व्यवहारगत परिवर्तन (SBC) का विशेषज्ञहरूसँगको सहकार्यले सन्देश प्रसारका अभियानहरू र अन्य MHPSS गतिविधिहरूको प्रभावकारिता बढाउन सक्छ। SBC मा व्यवहार र सामाजिक मान्यताहरूलाई आकार दिने संज्ञानात्मक, सामाजिक र संरचनागत कारकहरू बुझ्न र तिनलाई सम्बोधन गर्न सामाजिक विज्ञान र प्रमाणको प्रयोग गरिन्छ। सञ्चार, सामाजिक परिचालन र सामुदायिक सहभागिता जस्ता विभिन्न दृष्टिकोणहरू प्रयोग गर्दै, SBC टोलीहरूले समुदायहरूको सशक्तीकरण र स्वामित्वलाई सुदृढ पार्नुका साथै समुदायका सदस्यहरूसँग सहकार्य गरी मनोवृत्ति, विश्वास र व्यवहार बुझ्ने, सकारात्मक परिवर्तन प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने, प्रतिक्रिया सङ्कलन गर्ने, अफवाहहरूलाई सम्बोधन गर्ने र मिलेर समाधानहरू तयार गर्ने काम गर्छन्। उदाहरणका लागि, चासोहरू, सूचनासम्बन्धी कमीहरू, सहयोगका विद्यमान स्रोतहरू र सामना गर्ने उपायहरू पहिचान गर्न अनलाइन तथा अफलाइन ‘सामाजिक सुनुवाइ’/प्रतिक्रिया सङ्कलनका अभ्यासहरू सञ्चालन गरिन्छन्। SBCC लाई कहिलेकाहीँ [Communication for Development] (C4D), [Communicating With Communities] (CWC) र [Community Engagement & Accountability] भनेर पनि चिनिन्छ।
rows.bt: 43 Collaboration with experts in social and behavioural change (SBC) can increase the effectiveness of message dissemination campaigns and other MHPSS activities. SBC uses social science and evidence to understand and address the cognitive, social and structural factors that shape behaviour and social norms. Using various approaches such as communication, social mobilization and community participation, SBC teams strengthen communities' empowerment and ownership and also work together with community members to understand attitudes, beliefs and behaviour, promote positive change, collect feedback, address rumours and develop solutions together. For example, online and offline ‘social listening’/feedback collection exercises are conducted to identify concerns, gaps in information, existing sources of support and coping measures. SBCC is also sometimes known as [Communication for Development] (C4D), [Communicating With Communities] (CWC) and [Community Engagement & Accountability].
rows.note: The source introduces SBC but switches to undefined SBCC in its final sentence without explaining their relationship; both acronyms are preserved, and coping terminology is drafted without a supplied frozen equivalent.
